Separate TAPP from Solution SF-ICP-MS (see Row 5a). Single-quadrupole (Q) detector; unit mass resolution; trace/major elemental concentrations in digested/dissolved samples. Excludes: TQ-ICP-MS/MS (triple quadrupole; MS/MS-specific metadata too distinct), SF-ICP-MS, MC-ICP-MS, LA-coupled variants, and ICP-OES. CRC (collision/reaction cell) parameters — He KED, reactive gas DRC/CRC modes — are Q-specific and central to interference management strategy; no mode flag columns (single-mode technique). Architecture decision 2026-06-15: separate from SF because CRC fields would be dead-ends in an SF TAPP, and resolution mode fields would be trivial constants in a Q TAPP. LA-Q/SF-ICP-MS stays combined (CRC absent from all 13 assessed LA procedures). 4 seed papers confirmed (Solution Q-ICP-MS/ folder).

column4: HR-ICP-MS; single-collector sector-field ICP-MS (SF-ICP-MS); solution mode
column9: Separate TAPP from Solution Q-ICP-MS (see Row 5). Single-collector sector-field (SF) detector; selectable mass resolution (low ~300 / medium ~4000 / high ~10 000 m/Δm) resolves polyatomic interferences without CRC. Trace/major elemental concentrations in digested/dissolved samples. Excludes: Q-ICP-MS, TQ-ICP-MS/MS, MC-ICP-MS, LA-coupled variants, and ICP-OES. No mode flag columns (single-mode technique; mass resolution setting is an analyte-specific field value, not a separate mode). SF-specific fields include: mass resolution setting per analyte, SEM–Faraday detector cross-calibration. Architecture decision 2026-06-15 (see Row 5 notes). Seed papers TBD.
Separate from solution ICP-MS due to distinct measurement goals (isotope ratios vs. concentrations) and metadata (cup configuration, mass bias correction, reference standards).

column5: Elemental + isotopic composition (in situ, spatially resolved)
column9: Covers both quadrupole and single-collector sector-field instruments coupled to laser ablation for multi-element trace/major chemistry. Scope is trace element analysis only — LA-SF-ICP-MS U–Pb geochronology is a separate future TAPP (see Row 7d). Excludes MC and TQ/ToF mass analyzers, which require dedicated TAPPs. Most common LA-ICP-MS configuration in meteoritics literature. TAPP v4.1 complete (110 fields); Phase 2/3 literature assessment complete against 13 protocols from 10 papers. Technique renamed from LA-ICP-MS to LA-Q/SF-ICP-MS during development; current file is LA-Q:SF-ICP-MS/LA-Q:SF-ICPMS_TAPP_v4.1.csv — the LA-ICP-MS/LA-ICPMS_TAPP_v13.csv folder is a stale, frozen branch, not a separate TAPP.

column5: Isotopic composition (high-precision, in situ, spatially resolved)
column9: Multi-collector sector-field instrument coupled to laser ablation. Distinct from LA-Q/SF-ICP-MS due to multi-collector Faraday cup configuration, mass bias correction methods, and isotope-ratio-focused workflows (e.g., in situ Rb-Sr, Lu-Hf, U-Pb). Future TAPP; 1 seed paper identified (Zhang 2022, in situ Rb-Sr).

column5: Elemental composition (simultaneous full-spectrum, in situ, spatially resolved)
column9: Time-of-flight mass analyzer coupled to laser ablation. Unique capability: simultaneous acquisition of the full mass spectrum at each laser shot, enabling rapid multi-element imaging. Distinct metadata: no sequential mass scanning, spectral resolution, transient signal handling. Future TAPP; 1 seed paper identified (Chernonozhkin 2024, micrometeorite element mapping).

column5: Elemental composition (REE and interference-prone analytes, in situ)
column9: Triple quadrupole (ICP-MS/MS) coupled to laser ablation. Key distinct metadata: reaction cell gas identity and flow, MS/MS operational mode (mass-shift vs. on-mass), reaction product ions monitored. Important for accurate REE and transition-metal determination with polyatomic interference removal. Future TAPP; 1 seed paper identified (Masuda 2024, CAI REE mapping with iCAP TQ in KED mode).

column4: LA-SF-ICP-MS (single-collector sector-field) for in-situ U–Pb isotope dating
column9: Separate from LA-Q/SF-ICP-MS (trace elements) due to distinct data product (isotopic age vs. elemental concentration), data reduction philosophy (down-hole fractionation correction, common-Pb correction, Concordia age calculation), calibration standards (mineral-matched primary: GJ-1, 91500, Plešovice), and QC metrics (concordance %, MSWD). SF-specific hardware central to this application: E-scan mode at fixed magnet, SEM triple mode (pulse/analog/Faraday), per-isotope asymmetric dwell times (e.g., 2 ms for ²⁰²Hg, 30 ms for ²⁰⁷Pb), enhancement N₂ addition. Q-ICP-MS not standard for this application due to sensitivity constraints and Hg/Pb isobar complexity at unit resolution. Shared Group 1–3 laser and plasma hardware fields must be kept consistent with LA-Q/SF-ICP-MS TAPP per cross-TAPP propagation rule. 5 seed papers identified in LA-Q:SF-ICP-MS/LA-SF-ICP-MS/ folder: Frei & Gerdes 2009 (Chem. Geol.); Eckelmann et al. 2014 (Gondwana Res.); Lana et al. 2021 (Geostand. Geoanal. Res.); Wei et al. 2022 (JAAS); Yang et al. 2020 (JAAS). Future TAPP — not yet in development.

column5: Physical (3D internal structure, porosity, density distribution)
column9: Critical for 3D texture and porosity. Development split: Lab-XCT (industrial/geological microfocus CT) TAPP in progress (v5). SR-XCT and NCT to be developed separately. Preclinical/medical CT classification (e.g., GE eXplore) deferred for future review.

column4: Neutron CT; X-ray CT (simultaneous dual-modality acquisition)
column5: Physical (3D internal structure, density distribution, elemental/isotopic contrast)
column9: TENTATIVE — status to be revisited based on community feedback and technique availability. Covers simultaneous NCT+XCT acquisition on dual-modality platforms (e.g., NIST-NeXT NXCT). Distinct from sequential or separate NCT and Lab-XCT procedures: simultaneous acquisition produces intrinsically co-registered volumes in a single session, making two-TAPP registration with Coupled fields architecturally awkward. A combined TAPP would cover XCT-specific fields, NCT-specific fields (neutron source, wavelength, neutron detector), and coupling-specific fields (co-registration geometry). Not developed until standalone Lab-XCT and NCT TAPPs are finalized; lower priority given narrow current facility availability.
